entries.name: Joan Baez

expected_cases.charges: Blocking entrance to Armed Forces Induction Center (civil disobedience)
expected_cases.convicted: Arrested and jailed for blocking draft induction
expected_cases.sentence: Arrested in 1967 in Oakland during demonstrations at the Armed Forces Induction Center, where protesters sought to block draft processing. Served jail time as a consequence of the antiwar civil disobedience.

case.charges: Blocking the Oakland Armed Forces Induction Center during December 1967 anti-draft protests
case.sentence: Separate December 1967 anti-draft imprisonment at Santa Rita. The official chronology records a 90-day sentence with 45 days suspended. The Bay Area Television Archive describes her January 18, 1968 release press conference and separately reports 31 days served. The admission day is unresolved; December is recorded at month precision, and 31 days is the reported actual duration, not an inferred calendar interval. This is separate from the October 16-26, 1967 stay.

entries.rationale: Add second stay separately. Official chronology and December film document rearrest; January 18 press-conference description establishes release, though library film-date field is January 19. January 22 archive description explicitly reports 31 days; its unrelated tax-lawsuit filing-year typo is not used. No exact December day inferred.
